readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckJetLinearization.hasFDerivAt_evolution
readback.mathematical_statement: E is the fixed real three-dimensional Euclidean space ClosedSmoothModel 3. Bilin is E ->L[R] E ->L[R] R, Jet1 is E ->L[R] Bilin, Jet2 is E ->L[R] Jet1, and Variables is exactly (Bilin times Jet1) times Jet2. Thus a variable or variation is a nested pair ((G,J),H), with H's first two vector slots being its successive derivative-direction slots and its last two slots the bilinear-form arguments. The declaration has no universe parameters. Its local-instance preamble explicitly selects the standard Mathlib CLM normed additive groups and real normed spaces for Jet1, Jet2, and the background bilinear and trilinear E-valued map spaces, using real source and target scalars and RingHom.id R. It also selects the canonical Prod.normedAddCommGroup and Prod.normedSpace for Bilin times Jet1 and for Variables, and caches AddCommMonoid (Bilin times Jet1) as Prod.instAddCommMonoid. The product additive monoid has the usual componentwise addition and zero; this is an explicit canonical structure selection, not an extra hypothesis or a different algebraic operation. All norms, scalar actions, and product topologies are the original CLM operator-norm and standard product structures. In particular Jet2 has its existing operator norm as E ->L[R] Jet1. No alternative module, Matrix norm, or new mathematical premise is introduced. Fix arbitrary background maps B : E ->L[R] E ->L[R] E and DB : E ->L[R] E ->L[R] E ->L[R] E, an arbitrary G0 in Bilin, J0 in Jet1, and H0 in Jet2. Assume only G0.IsInvertible, meaning G0 : E -> E dual is the forward map of a continuous real-linear equivalence. G0 need not be symmetric or positive-definite; J0 and H0 need not be realized first and second derivatives or satisfy slot symmetries; B and DB need not be realized background field/derivative data. For G in Bilin, let K(G)_(i,j) = G(e_i)(e_j), where e_i = basis3 i is the standard Euclidean basis. Let a(G) = inverseEntries G, the actual full Matrix.inv of this 3 by 3 coordinate matrix. The pinned principal map is principal G H = the double sum over i,j : Fin 3 of a(G)_(i,j) smul H(e_i)(e_j), a Bilin-valued contraction. The actual finite-jet evolution map with B and DB fixed is evolution B DB ((G,J),H) = principal G H + DeTurckPrincipalIdentity.lowerTerm B DB G J. The lower term is the existing actual Bilin-valued Ricci/Lie first-jet expression, not an existential or approximate lower witness. The theorem first asserts HasFDerivAt of this evolution map at ((G0,J0),H0), with derivative equal to the pinned constructed continuous real-linear map differential B DB G0 J0 H0 : Variables ->L[R] Bilin. No derivative map is supplied as a hypothesis. The derivative map is explicitly constructed as the sum of three CLM expressions: the sum over i,j of inverseEntryDerivative G0 i j, multiplied via smulRight by H0(e_i)(e_j) and composed with metricProjection; the sum over i,j of a(G0)_(i,j) smul secondJetEvaluation i j; and lowerDifferential B DB G0 J0 composed with the first product projection Variables -> Bilin times Jet1. The pinned metricProjection sends h=((hG,hJ),hH) to hG=h.1.1. The pinned secondJetEvaluation i j sends h to hH(e_i)(e_j)=h.2(e_i)(e_j), in that order. lowerDifferential B DB G0 J0 is the actual fderiv R at (G0,J0) of (G,J) |-> lowerTerm B DB G J, a continuous real-linear map on Bilin times Jet1; it is not a chosen abstract lower derivative. Its application here is to h.1=(hG,hJ). The theorem additionally states the explicit scalar value of the constructed differential for every arbitrary h in Variables and every v,w in E. Write a0=a(G0). That value is the sum over all i,j of a0_(i,j) * hH(e_i)(e_j)(v)(w), plus the sum over all i,j of [-sum over all k,l of a0_(i,k) * hG(e_k)(e_l) * a0_(l,j)] * H0(e_i)(e_j)(v)(w), plus lowerDifferential B DB G0 J0 (hG,hJ)(v)(w). Both outer i,j sums range over every pair in Fin 3, and the inverse-variation inner sum includes every k,l pair in Fin 3. The inverse-variation term retains the minus sign and both inverse factors, with the coordinate variation hG in between. It is contracted against the frozen second jet H0, so the required Da(G0)[hG] applied to H0 contribution is present. The separate hH term is the second-jet variation against the frozen inverse coefficients. No index transposition, symmetric-index reduction, or omission of the first-jet direction hJ is made. The three contributions enter with addition because evolution is principal plus lowerTerm. B and DB are fixed during this derivative certificate; there are no hB or hDB components in Variables. The scalar formula and the derivative certificate are both conclusions for the same actual constructed differential. The statement is an ordinary real finite-dimensional Frechet derivative and its full pointwise tensor-slot formula, local at invertible G0. It does not impose a time interval, Hoelder exponent, manifold, chart-source or cutoff condition, spatial coefficient field, actual metric family, flow, quantitative coefficient bound, or assumed linear operator package. It does not itself identify arbitrary jets with geometric chart evolution, prove spatial regularity or differentiated tensor covariance, construct bounded global L=dt-DQ(g0), establish its global signed residual/contraction with P, or produce physical Ricci flow, Hamilton convergence, smoothability, or the final Poincare theorem.
